summary: Global search, filters and ranking. A new search module holds the two rules that decide what a visitor sees: which records a typed term finds, and in what order matching records are shown. The order is the five bands of §15 — PROMOTED, TRUSTED, VERIFIED, COMPLETE, BASE — implemented as bands rather than a score, so no pair of lower axes ever overtakes a higher band, and inside a band the order stays neutral and alphabetical. An advertising package reaches the top band only through promotedWhenRelevant, the single path to it: a record that does not match the term, the place or the topic is not in the result set at all, so an irrelevant advertisement buys no placement. Every answer and the page itself carry RANKING_VERSION, so an order a visitor saw can be traced to the rule that produced it. Spelling tolerance forgives one edit per word on words of at least four characters, matched word by word: matching the whole typed phrase as one run of letters had made two different names a single edit apart into the same search, which the database test caught and the rule now prevents. A geographic or professional filter is answered only by the directories, because a breed page or an article has no city and no licence, and the page says plainly which kinds were left out and why. The three public directories now rank by the same bands and show the «تبلیغ» label, so one rule orders every list. /search is not a §4 section: it is its own public route, opened from a header search box, carrying its whole query in the address and published with a new noindex option in buildMetadata, since a search page is a view of other pages rather than a page of its own.

limitations: No real search index: all six sources are read and ranked in memory with a 500-record ceiling per source, exactly as the existing directories already worked; moving them behind one indexed query is a database change of its own.

Spelling tolerance is one edit per word on words of four characters or more — not transliteration, phonetics or synonyms; a breed's English name comes from the breed bank and alternative names are matched only in that source.
Ordering inside a band is alphabetical: no quality signal, geographic distance or recency enters the order, because none of them is defined in the sources.
Autocomplete and «near me» were not built; neither is asked for in the sources.
Browser and unit/DB checks were targeted by user instruction; unaffected suites were last run in full at commit 7c74577.
